PLUS tan accepts decimal inputs very close to 90deg/100grad; exact poles error and Back returns before the function close. Both signs and both sides of the pole, MathI/LineI and correction from tan(pi/2) to tan(pi/3) measured.
Degree/Grad sin/cos reduce the period in decimal rational space before conversion. 8999999999deg and 9999999999grad are valid; 9000000000deg, 1e10grad and 157079632.7rad error.

Near-pole Degree/Grad tangent uses the decimal difference from an odd half-turn then cotangent. Radian literal arithmetic uses a high precision mathematical pi constant for the difference before binary conversion; independent inputs 1.5707963268, 1.57079632679, its negative and 4.7123889804 match. Symbolic pi and memory/SOLVE paths retain their existing handling. No claim about every hidden digit or every computed near-pole expression.
Explicit degree/grad suffixes under Radian and radian suffix under Degree measured. sin(30deg)=1/2, sin(50grad)=sqrt(2)/2, cos(pi rad)=-1. Small nonzero sin(1e-8deg)=1.745329252e-10 remains nonzero.
